desc: Parse input (N, M, X and M edges) and build two adjacency lists: forward edges and reversed edges.
Implement Dijkstra over states (v, dir) with dist array of size 2 x (N+1), initialized to infinity except dist[0][1] = 0.
For each popped state, relax neighbors: move along adjacency list corresponding to current orientation with cost 1, and flip orientation at same vertex with cost X.
Use a binary heap (priority queue) with lazy deletion via stale-distance checks; ensure 64-bit distances (Python ints are fine).
Compute answer as min(dist[0][N], dist[1][N]) and print it.
Verify complexity O((N + M) log N) fits constraints, and sanity-check logic against the provided samples mentally (e.g., sample 2 gives 3 via one reversal).
